questions.question: To keep normal braking power, drivers with a front brake limiting valve should:

options.text: Set the control to the off position.
Set the control to the neutral position.

questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Setting it to "slippery" reduces stopping power. Always keep the valve set to "normal" for full braking power.

questions.question: When driving long distances, take a break ____ to avoid fatigue.
questions.explanation: Stop for a break at least every two hours or every 100 miles to prevent fatigue during a long trip.

questions.question: A skid caused by pressing the accelerator too hard can be fixed by:

options.text: Removing your foot from the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Removing your foot from the accelerator.
questions.explanation: Release the accelerator to stop a skid caused by over-acceleration. This type of skid happens most often on snow or ice.

questions.question: A wig wag is:

options.text: A low air pressure warning device.
A tube that carries air to the brakes.
A type of air brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: A low air pressure warning device.
questions.explanation: Air brake vehicles must have a low air pressure warning device. A wig wag drops a mechanical arm into your view if air pressure drops between 55 and 75 psi.

questions.question: When entering a foggy area, you should:

options.text: Stop on the side of the roadway.

questions.explanation: Slow down when entering fog. Use low beam headlights, do not pass other vehicles, and do not stop on the roadway. The safest choice is to avoid driving in fog if possible.

questions.question: Regrooved tires:

options.text: Should not be used on any vehicle.
Should not be used on the front of a bus.
Should not be used on trucks hauling gravel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used on the front of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires are not allowed on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: When should cargo securement be checked after starting a trip?
questions.explanation: Check cargo before starting, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo safely secured throughout the trip.

questions.question: Backing with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks do not have the ability to go in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Only reverse if absolutely necessary.

questions.question: If brakes fail on a steep downhill slope, the driver should:

options.text: Turn the vehicle off and then back on to reset the brakes.
Look for an escape ramp or another way to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for an escape ramp or another way to stop.
questions.explanation: Use an escape ramp if your brakes fail on a downhill slope. If no escape ramp is available, look for another escape route, such as a side road or open field.

questions.question: Steering wheel movement of more than ____ can make steering difficult.
questions.explanation: A steering wheel should have no more than 10 degrees of play, or about two inches of movement on a 20-inch wheel. More play than this makes steering difficult.

questions.question: Where should your vehicle end up during a basic vehicle controls skills test?

options.text: Somewhere near where the examiner said.
Within three feet of where the examiner said.

questions.explanation: You must park your vehicle in the exact spot the examiner tells you to. If you don't, you may fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: In cold weather, how often should you check and fill an alcohol evaporator?
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator stops ice from forming in air brake systems. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: When should you turn off a retarder for safety?

options.text: When the roads are wet, snowy, or icy.
When you are carrying a heavy load.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the roads are wet, snowy, or icy.
questions.explanation: A retarder helps slow your vehicle and reduces brake use. But it can cause your wheels to skid on slippery roads. Turn off the retarder when roads are wet, snowy, or icy.

questions.question: When should you test your service brakes?
questions.explanation: Always test your brakes before you drive. This helps you find problems before you need to brake on the road.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to spot vehicle problems?

options.text: Only checking things at the start and end of your trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only checking things at the start and end of your trip.
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle often during trips. Watch the gauges, look in mirrors, and check tires, cargo, and lights. Use all your senses to spot early signs of trouble.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Jump directly from your seat to the ground.
Keep at least one hand on the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Face your vehicle and keep three points of contact while leaving. On a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: What should you look for under your vehicle before driving?
questions.explanation: Look under your vehicle for oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks on the ground. These signs mean your vehicle needs repairs before you drive it.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal must be:

options.text: Not used on air brake vehicles.

questions.explanation: Every vehicle with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal.

questions.question: What should you check during a pre-trip inspection?
questions.explanation: Check the engine oil level, coolant level, and hose condition during a pre-trip inspection.

questions.question: A convex mirror is sometimes called a ____ mirror.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles use curved, convex mirrors called "fisheye," "spot," or "bug-eye" mirrors. They show a wider view than flat mirrors but make objects look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: When accelerating on a slippery surface like a wet road, a driver should:

options.text: Not worry about the road surface.

questions.explanation: Accelerate slowly when driving on slippery surfaces. This helps you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Brakes may get out of adjustment:
questions.explanation: Brakes can quickly go out of adjustment if they overheat from heavy use. Check your brake adjustment frequently.

questions.question: A vehicle must be equipped with all of the following, except:

options.text: Warning devices for a parked vehicle.

questions.explanation: Commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, warning triangles or flares, and a fire extinguisher. A flashlight is not required.

questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, you:

options.text: Must maintain four points of contact with the vehicle.
May face the road before fully exiting.
Must face away from the vehicle.

questions.explanation: When exiting, always face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. For buses, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may result in failing the vehicle control test.

questions.question: The two indicators that determine when you should upshift are:

options.text: Oil pressure and air brake pressure.

questions.explanation: Watch two things to know when to shift up. First is engine speed (rpm) — check your manual for the correct range. Second is road speed (mph) — check your speedometer and shift as needed.

questions.question: What is black ice?

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road.
A thin layer of ice on the road.
Ice that is black from dirt on the road.
Ice that is easy to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin layer of ice on the road.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see through it to the road below. A road with black ice may look like it is just wet.

questions.question: A driver should always:
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead for hazards. Plan what you would do if each hazard becomes dangerous.

questions.question: One way to prevent fatigue on long trips is to:
questions.explanation: Take a break every 100 miles or every 2 hours of driving. Driving at night or during your normal sleep time increases the risk of fatigue.

questions.question: In cold weather, check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator:
questions.explanation: The alcohol evaporator prevents ice buildup in air brake systems. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: When double clutching, if you stay in neutral too long and cannot shift to the next gear, you should:

options.text: Stop the vehicle and start over.
Return to neutral, release the clutch, increase speed, and try again.
Skip the intended gear and shift to the next one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to neutral, release the clutch, increase speed, and try again.
questions.explanation: If you stay in neutral too long and have trouble shifting, do not force it. Return to neutral, release the clutch, speed up to match the road speed, and try again.

questions.question: When entering a curve, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down to a safe speed and shift into a lower gear before entering a curve.

questions.question: While driving, your mirrors:

options.text: Should only be used when changing lanes.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while driving. This helps you see traffic around you and spot problems with your vehicle.

questions.question: Windshield wiper blades should be:
questions.explanation: Check wiper blades for damage and stiff rubber. Keep the blades clean and make sure they are secure.

questions.question: When a vehicle is started, the coolant temperature should:
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, the coolant temperature should gradually increase to the normal operating range.

questions.question: If something is found to be unsafe during a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Continue with the trip and make an appointment with a mechanic after the trip is completed.
Let a more experienced driver use the truck.
Not use the items found to be unsafe, but may continue driving normally.

questions.explanation: You must fix any safety problems found during inspection. It is illegal to drive an unsafe vehicle.

questions.question: An example of required emergency equipment is:
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must carry emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, reflective triangles or flares, and a fire extinguisher.

questions.question: In a leaf spring:
questions.explanation: Check that leaf springs have no missing or broken leaves. If more than one-fourth of the leaves are missing, the vehicle must be taken out of service.

questions.question: While driving, if you notice anything that affects safety or could lead to mechanical problems, you should:

options.text: Wait to see if the problem goes away.
Include the concerns in your written report.
Try to fix the issue yourself.

questions.correctAnswerText: Include the concerns in your written report.
questions.explanation: Write down any safety issues or mechanical problems you notice while driving. Report these in your vehicle condition report at the end of the day.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out of the vehicle and call for assistance.
Continue trying to get your vehicle off the tracks until you are successful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and call for assistance.
questions.explanation: Leave your vehicle immediately and move away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information on the signal box and call 911 or the emergency number provided.

questions.question: When traveling with cargo, you must make sure the cargo is secure:

options.text: Every 150 miles or three hours of driving.
Only after traveling up a hill.
Only after coming to a hard stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles or three hours of driving.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every 150 miles or three hours of driving. You are responsible for keeping cargo secure throughout the trip.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: When driving down a hill, when should you shift into a lower gear?

options.text: As you begin to move downward
As you go downhill and pick up speed

questions.explanation: Shift into a lower gear before you start going downhill. If you wait, your brakes may overheat and fail.

questions.question: Drowsy driving happens most often during:
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving is most common at night because people are naturally less alert when they normally sleep. Take precautions to prevent fatigue when driving at night.

questions.question: If one air system in a dual air brake system has very low pressure:

options.text: None of the brakes will work at all.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There will be no noticeable effect.
Lights on the outside of the tractor will flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, if one system loses pressure, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully. Stop safely and have the system repaired.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a double combination vehicle is ____ per minute.
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle should have no more than 4 psi air loss per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal should activate when:
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning signal must activate when tank pressure falls below 60 psi. The warning can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: When it is hard for others to see your vehicle at dawn or dusk, you can help by:

options.text: Waving an arm out the window.

questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights to low beam when visibility is low. If you cannot see others, they cannot see you.

questions.question: The safety belt should:
questions.explanation: Check that your safety belt is secure, adjustable, latches properly, and is not ripped or frayed.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, what is the maximum safe leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should have no more than 3 psi air loss per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: What prevents wheel lockup when braking?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheels from locking up when brakes are applied.
